t: A fire of unknown cause broke out in Boston, Massachusetts, destroying 349 buildings.
Seven Years' War: France began an unsuccessful attempt to retake Quebec City, which had been captured by Britain.
The Williamsburg Bray School, the oldest-surviving school building in the U.S. dedicated to educating Black children, opened at Benjamin Franklin's suggestion.
In a treaty with Dutch colonial authorities, the Ndyuka people of Suriname gained territorial autonomy.
George III became King of Great Britain and Ireland, succeeding his grandfather George II.
The chapel of the newly constructed Castellania in Valletta, Malta, was consecrated.
